answer: An agent marketplace requires every identity, whether named atlas, vine, or pearl, to lock $100 for 30 days before it can bid on work. Each identity needs a separate deposit; funds cannot back two accounts at once. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore ties up $100,000. The marginal cost per fake is the financing cost of locking another $100 for a month, plus any deposit forfeited when that account submits a result that fails the job’s predefined verification test.
